To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ICAM-1 is a ligand of LFA-1 and that ICAM- 11 dimers have a higher binding avidity for LFA- 1 than monomers.
ICAM-1 forms dimers on the cell surface, and that the dimer is a better ligand for LFA- 1 than the monomer.
ICAM-1 forms homodimers and that these dimers are more effective ligands for the integrin LFA-1 than monomeric ICAM-1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of ICAM- 2, a member of the immunoglobulin gene superfamily of cell adhesion molecules.
the molecular mechanisms of adhesion between leukocytes and endothelial cells, and the role of adhesion in the development of inflammation and atherosclerosis.
the molecular basis of adhesion mediated by the lymphocyte function associated (LFA)-1 integrin, and its ligands, intercellular adhesion molecule- 1 (ICAM)-1 and ICAM-2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dimerization of the ectodomain is an important mechanism in regulating the function of ICAM- 11.
ICAM-1 dimerizes and that the dimerization of ICAM- 11 is important for the adhesion of LFA-1 to ICAM-1.
ICAM-1 is a dimeric ligand for the leukocyte integrin LFA-1 and this dimerization enhances LFA-1-mediated adhesion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ICAM-1 is a dimeric molecule that is capable of forming homotypic interactions.
ICAM-1 homodimerization is a key step in the formation of a high avidity LFA-1/ICAM-1 bond.
ICAM-1 dimerizes and this dimerization is important for the interaction of ICAM- 2 with LFA-1 and for the avidity of the LFA-1/ICAM-1 interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ICAM-1 is a homophilic ligand for LFA- 1 and that dimeric ICAM-1 binds to LFA-1 more avidly than does monomeric ICAM-1.
ICAM-1 dimer formation is a normal feature of the molecule, and that this dimerization is required for high affinity ligand binding.
ICAM-1 dimer formation is a key step in the regulation of LFA-1-mediated cell adhesion.
